https.title: HTTPS
https.description: TierPlan always serves HTTPS. See the certificate it is using, or get a free one from Let's Encrypt that browsers trust.

certificate.title: Certificate in use

note.self_signed: TierPlan made this certificate for this install. Browsers warn about it until you use Let's Encrypt or your own certificate files.

certificate.pausedNextFiles: Paused while certificate files are set

reason.default: This is the default. No certificate files and no Let's Encrypt certificate are set up.
reason.pending: Let's Encrypt is set up, but no certificate has been issued yet.
reason.envPending: TIERPLAN_ACME is on. TierPlan is getting a certificate by itself.
reason.stopped: Let's Encrypt is stopped. Issue a certificate to use it again.
reason.fallback: The Let's Encrypt certificate expired. TierPlan serves its own certificate until a renewal works.
reason.envOff: Let's Encrypt is turned off by TIERPLAN_ACME.
reason.files: Set by TIERPLAN_TLS_CERT_FILE and TIERPLAN_TLS_KEY_FILE. Certificate files take priority over Let's Encrypt.
reason.filesPaused: Set by TIERPLAN_TLS_CERT_FILE and TIERPLAN_TLS_KEY_FILE. Let's Encrypt is paused while they are set.
reason.issued: TierPlan got this certificate from Let's Encrypt and renews it.
reason.issuedEnv: Turned on by TIERPLAN_ACME. TierPlan renews it by itself.
reason.pausedRestore: Paused after a restore. Resume Let's Encrypt below to renew.

certFiles.title: Certificate files
certFiles.hstsYes: HSTS can be sent for it.
certFiles.hstsNo: HSTS is never sent for it.
certFiles.foot: TierPlan only reads these files and checks them again about once a minute, so a renewed certificate is picked up without a restart. To use Let's Encrypt, remove both variables and restart.

self_signed.fix: Use a certificate from a public certificate authority.

unknown_authority.sentence: It isn't signed by an authority this server trusts.
unknown_authority.fix: Use a certificate from a public authority. If it is, the file may be missing the intermediate certificates: put them after the certificate in the same file.

test_ca.sentence: It comes from a test certificate authority.
test_ca.fix: Test certificates aren't trusted by browsers.

expired.sentence: It has expired or isn't valid yet.

name_mismatch.fix: Get a certificate that includes {{host}}, or change the public URL in Settings > General.

no_public_url.sentence: No public URL is set, so TierPlan can't check the name.
no_public_url.fix: Set the public URL in Settings > General.

acme.title: Let's Encrypt
acme.description: Get a free certificate that browsers trust. TierPlan orders it, renews it by itself and switches to it without a restart. Nobody is signed out.
acme.portNote: Let's Encrypt checks your domain over plain HTTP on port 80. Port 80 on {{host}} must reach TierPlan, for example by starting the container with {{flag}}. TierPlan answers the check on its usual port, so there is nothing else to run.

http01.label: HTTP-01
http01.description: Let's Encrypt checks over plain HTTP on port 80. Port 80 on your public host must reach TierPlan.

dns01.label: DNS-01
dns01.description: TierPlan adds a TXT record at your DNS provider. No port needs opening, so it works for an install the internet can't reach.

suggest.title: DNS-01 may suit this install better
suggest.body: {{host}} points at a private address ({{address}}) as this server sees it. Let's Encrypt usually can't reach a private address, so HTTP-01 is likely to fail. DNS-01 doesn't need Let's Encrypt to reach TierPlan.

validation.helper: A change applies from the next order. The certificate in use stays as it is.

changed.title: Validation method changed
changed.renew: The certificate in use hasn't changed. TierPlan uses {{method}} from the next order. Renew now to test it.
changed.issue: No certificate has been ordered with {{method}} yet. Issue certificate to test it.

names.title: Names on the certificate
names.helper: The host of the public URL, plus the host of the agent URL when it is different. Change them in {{link}}. IP addresses and wildcards can't be used.
names.none: No public URL is set yet. Set it in {{link}}.

account.title: Account
account.empty: Let's Encrypt needs an account for this install. TierPlan keeps its key encrypted and never shows it.

email.label: Contact email (optional)
email.helper: Let's Encrypt uses it to reach you about problems with the account. You can leave it empty.
email.error: Enter a valid email address, or leave it empty.

terms.label: I agree to the Let's Encrypt {{link}}
terms.error: Accept the Subscriber Agreement to register.

account.keyNote: TierPlan keeps the account key encrypted and never shows it.

profile.label: Certificate profile
profile.helper: The default is right for most installs. A profile sets how long certificates last and what they are for. It applies from the next order and doesn't change the certificate in use.
profile.none: This directory offers no profiles. The CA default is used.
profile.unreadable: Let's Encrypt's list of profiles couldn't be read. You can still save the profile shown.

setup.intro: Create a Cloudflare API token with two permissions: {{edit}} and {{read}}. Limit it to the zones your certificate names are in. TierPlan doesn't accept the Global API Key. Create it on {{link}}.
setup.records: For each check TierPlan adds a TXT record at _acme-challenge and deletes it afterwards. It only deletes records it created.

token.label: Cloudflare API token
token.helper: TierPlan keeps the token encrypted and never shows it again. To change it, enter a new one.
token.savedNote: TierPlan keeps it encrypted and never shows it.
token.kept: Kept for DNS-01. TierPlan keeps it encrypted and never shows it.

remove.unavailable: To remove the token, switch to HTTP-01 and save first. Removing it now would stop renewals.
remove.title: Remove the Cloudflare token?
remove.body: TierPlan deletes the saved token. You'll need to enter a token again to use DNS-01. Certificates already issued are not affected.
remove.leftOver_one: TierPlan needs the token to delete the {{count}} TXT record it left in Cloudflare. Remove it now and it stays there until you delete it yourself.
remove.leftOver_other: TierPlan needs the token to delete the {{count}} TXT records it left in Cloudflare. Remove it now and they stay there until you delete them yourself.

resolvers.label: DNS resolvers (optional)
resolvers.helper: Comma-separated, each as host or host:port. When set, TierPlan asks only these while it waits for a record to appear. Leave it empty to ask the zone's own nameservers, which is right for most installs.
resolvers.delegation: If {{name}} is a CNAME, TierPlan follows it and writes the record at the target. The target must be in a Cloudflare zone this token can edit. There is nothing to set.
resolvers.error: {{entry}} isn't a valid resolver. Use host or host:port, separated by commas.
resolvers.errorList: The resolver list isn't valid. Use host or host:port, separated by commas, with at most five.

test.helper: Test token checks the names above without placing an order. It adds a test TXT record at each name and deletes it again.
test.hint: This can take a minute while TierPlan waits for the record to appear.
test.required: Enter a Cloudflare API token to test.

result.notSaved: Nothing was saved. The settings in use are unchanged.
result.stale: This result is for earlier settings. Test again.

row.delegatedOwnZone: {{zone}} is not on Cloudflare. Delegated to {{target}}.
row.deleteKept: TierPlan keeps trying to delete it. See the left-over records below.

info.notSeenHint: The token works, so this didn't fail the test. An order waits for the record to appear and can time out. Check that this host can reach {{resolvers}} on port 53, or set resolvers under Advanced DNS.

dns_token_invalid.headline: Cloudflare didn't accept the API token.
dns_token_invalid.fix: The token is wrong, expired or revoked. Create a new token and enter it again under Validation method.

dns_token_scope.headline: The Cloudflare token can't manage DNS records for {{host}}.
dns_token_scope.fix: The token needs both Zone:DNS:Edit and Zone:Zone:Read, and it must include the zone for {{host}}. Fix it in Cloudflare, or enter a new token.

dns_zone_not_found.headline: Cloudflare has no zone for {{host}}.
dns_zone_not_found.fix: Add the zone to the Cloudflare account the token belongs to, and check that the token includes it. Or make _acme-challenge.{{host}} a CNAME to a record in a Cloudflare zone you can edit.

dns_delegation_target.headline: _acme-challenge.{{host}} is delegated to {{target}}, which TierPlan can't edit.
dns_delegation_target.fix: The target must be in a Cloudflare zone this token can edit. Add that zone to the token, or change the CNAME.

dns_not_visible.headline: The TXT record for {{host}} didn't appear on {{resolvers}}.
dns_not_visible.fix: Check that this host can reach {{resolvers}} on port 53. If you set resolvers under Advanced DNS, they must answer for public records. Clear them to ask the zone's own nameservers.

dns_rate_limited.headline: Cloudflare is limiting requests.
dns_rate_limited.fix: TierPlan waits until {{time}} before it tries again. There is nothing to do.
dns_rate_limited.fixNoTime: TierPlan waits before it tries again. There is nothing to do.

dns_unavailable.headline: Cloudflare couldn't be reached.
dns_unavailable.fix: TierPlan tries again on its own schedule, next at {{time}}. If it keeps failing, check this host's internet access.
dns_unavailable.fixNoTime: TierPlan tries again on its own schedule. If it keeps failing, check this host's internet access.

validation_txt.headline: Let's Encrypt didn't find the right TXT record for _acme-challenge.{{host}}.
validation_txt.fix: TierPlan saw the record, but Let's Encrypt didn't. Check that the zone's nameservers at your registrar are Cloudflare's, and that nothing else at _acme-challenge.{{host}} gets in the way, such as a conflicting CNAME. Then try again.

rate_limited.headline: Let's Encrypt is limiting requests.
rate_limited.fix: TierPlan waits until {{time}} before it tries again. There is nothing to do.
rate_limited.fixNoTime: TierPlan waits before it tries again. There is nothing to do.

validation_unreachable.headline: Let's Encrypt couldn't reach http://{{host}}/.well-known/acme-challenge/.
validation_unreachable.fix: Port 80 on {{host}} must reach TierPlan, for example with -p 80:{{port}}. Check your firewall and router, then try again.

validation_dns.headline: The DNS records for {{host}} don't point at this host.
validation_dns.fix: Make the A and AAAA records for {{host}} point at this host. Remove an old AAAA record if you have no IPv6. Then try again.

caa_forbids.headline: A CAA record forbids Let's Encrypt for {{host}}.
caa_forbids.fix: Add a CAA record that allows letsencrypt.org, or remove the one that blocks it.

identifier_rejected.headline: Let's Encrypt won't issue for {{host}}.
identifier_rejected.fix: Use a public DNS name under a domain you own as the public URL.

contact_invalid.headline: Let's Encrypt rejected the contact email.
contact_invalid.fix: Register again with a valid address, or leave it empty.

tos_action_required.headline: Let's Encrypt changed its terms.
tos_action_required.fix: Read the current terms at {{url}}, then try again.

account_gone.headline: Let's Encrypt doesn't know this account.
account_gone.fix: Register the account again in the Account section.

profile_invalid.headline: Let's Encrypt doesn't offer the profile {{profile}}.
profile_invalid.fix: Choose another profile under Advanced, or go back to the CA default.

ca_unavailable.headline: Let's Encrypt couldn't be reached.
ca_unavailable.fix: TierPlan tries again on its own schedule, next at {{time}}. If it keeps failing, check this host's internet access.
ca_unavailable.fixNoTime: TierPlan tries again on its own schedule. If it keeps failing, check this host's internet access.

ca_untrusted.headline: TierPlan doesn't trust the certificate authority's certificate.
ca_untrusted.fix: This only happens with a test directory. Check TIERPLAN_ACME_CA_FILE.

internal.headline: Something went wrong inside TierPlan.
internal.fix: Open Details and check the server log. TierPlan tries again at {{time}}.
internal.fixNoTime: Open Details and check the server log.

issue.helper: TierPlan switches to the new certificate as soon as it is ready. Nothing restarts and nobody is signed out.
issue.noAccount: Register a Let's Encrypt account first.
issue.runActive: A run is already in progress.
issue.toldToWait: Let's Encrypt asked TierPlan to wait. You can try again at {{time}}.
issue.failureGuard: Three attempts failed in the last hour. TierPlan waits so it doesn't use up Let's Encrypt's limits. You can try again at {{time}}.
issue.reused: These names already have a valid certificate until {{date}}. Nothing was ordered. Use Renew now to get a new one.

names_ip.reason: The public URL uses an IP address ({{host}}).
names_ip.fix: Set the public URL in Settings > General to a DNS name that points to this host.

agent_url_ip.reason: The agent URL uses an IP address ({{host}}).
agent_url_ip.fix: Set the agent URL to a DNS name, or clear it to use the public URL.

names_wildcard.fix: Use a plain host name. Wildcard certificates aren't supported.

names_not_public.reason: {{host}} isn't a public DNS name. It has no dot, or ends in a private suffix such as .lan or .home.arpa.
names_not_public.fix: Use a name under a domain you own, such as tierplan.example.com. Nothing was sent to Let's Encrypt.

base_path.reason: The public URL has a path ({{path}}).
base_path.fix: HTTP-01 needs TierPlan at the root of its host. Remove the path from the public URL, or give TierPlan its own host name.

agent_dial_host.reason_one: {{count}} connected agent reaches TierPlan at {{hosts}}, which isn't on the certificate.
agent_dial_host.reason_other: {{count}} connected agents reach TierPlan at {{hosts}}, which isn't on the certificate.
agent_dial_host.fix: Reinstall those agents with a new install command, or set the agent URL to the host they use. Only agents that are connected now are checked.

run.validUntil: Now serving a certificate valid until {{date}}.

hint.challenge: Serving the HTTP-01 token on port 80.
hint.challengeDns01: Adding the TXT record {{record}} at Cloudflare.
hint.challengeDns01Delegated: Adding the TXT record {{record}} at Cloudflare. _acme-challenge.{{host}} is delegated to {{target}}.
hint.validate: Waiting for Let's Encrypt to check {{host}}.
hint.stored: Saving the certificate and switching to it.
hint.cleanup: Removing the TXT records TierPlan added.
hint.cleanupLeftOver_one: Couldn't remove {{count}} record. TierPlan keeps trying. See the left-over records above.
hint.cleanupLeftOver_other: Couldn't remove {{count}} records. TierPlan keeps trying. See the left-over records above.

leftover.title_one: A TXT record is left in Cloudflare
leftover.title_other: {{count}} TXT records are left in Cloudflare
leftover.intro: TierPlan couldn't delete these records it created. It keeps trying and removes them as soon as it can. The order itself was not affected.
leftover.pausedRestore: Retries are paused until you resume Let's Encrypt.
leftover.pausedCertFiles: Retries are paused while TIERPLAN_TLS_CERT_FILE and TIERPLAN_TLS_KEY_FILE are set.
leftover.footer: You can also delete a record yourself in the Cloudflare dashboard. TierPlan's records have a comment that starts with {{prefix}}.

basis.two_thirds: Two thirds through the certificate's life
basis.half: Half way through the certificate's life

alerts.certFilesOnly: Remove TIERPLAN_TLS_CERT_FILE and TIERPLAN_TLS_KEY_FILE to use Let's Encrypt.

certFilesKept.title: Paused by certificate files
certFilesKept.body: Let's Encrypt is paused because TIERPLAN_TLS_CERT_FILE and TIERPLAN_TLS_KEY_FILE are set. TierPlan keeps your Let's Encrypt certificate, order and account. Remove both variables and restart to pick them up again.

restore.title: Paused after restore
restore.body: This instance was restored from a backup. TierPlan makes no Let's Encrypt requests until you resume, so a copy can't use up the original's limits. The certificate being served is unchanged.

namesChanged.title: The names have changed
namesChanged.body: The certificate covers {{old}}. The public URL and agent URL now need {{new}}. TierPlan keeps renewing the old names until you issue again.

fallback.title: Serving the self-signed certificate
fallback.body: The Let's Encrypt certificate expired on {{date}} because renewal kept failing. TierPlan is serving its self-signed certificate until a renewal works, and keeps trying. Browsers warn about it. Agents that use the self-signed pin stay connected.

testDirectory.title: Test certificate authority
testDirectory.body: TIERPLAN_ACME_DIRECTORY_URL is set, so TierPlan talks to {{url}} instead of Let's Encrypt. This is for testing only and isn't supported. Certificates from it aren't trusted by browsers.

stop.title: Stop using Let's Encrypt?
stop.body: TierPlan goes back to its own self-signed certificate right away, with no restart, and stops renewing. Browsers will warn again. Agents that use the self-signed pin keep working. Your Let's Encrypt account is kept, so you can issue again with one click.
